newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech fund IPF KB seeks share buyback approval.
newsitem.headline: Czech fund IPF KB seeks share buyback approval.

text.p: Managers of the Czech investment fund Investicni Privatizacni Fond Komercni Banky a.s. said on Friday they would seek approval from shareholders in September for mangagement to buy back shares in order to boost the share price.

"The main topic of the (extraordinary) shareholders' meeting will be approval for buying back the fund's shares with the aim of supporting the price of the shares on the public markets," the fund's managers IKS KB a.s. said in a statement.

The fund, managed by Investicni Kapitalova Spolecnost KB, the investment arm of the largest Czech commercial bank Komercni Banka a.s., said the plan would result in reducing the huge discount at which fund shares have been trading.
The last available records show that the IPF shares traded at a 46.3 percent discount on July 11.
IPF said the buyback, if approved, would only be conducted through the Prague Stock Exchange's automated trading system.
It did not say how many shares the fund intended to buy.
IPF shares, one of the Prague Stock Exchange's 11 continuously traded issues, lost 13 crowns on Thursday to close at 477. The stock has lost some 40 percent since February.
